committed: Before any implementation output was inspected: this file and the validation contract in OVERLAYS.md were committed ahead of js/measure/overlay.js, the oracle's inputs and results and every measurement. A check that a measurement crosses is a failed check, not a reason to move the bound; no bound is multiplied or relaxed after a result is seen; only Carl resets one, with a register row.

conventions.pixels: FITS: 1 is the centre of the first pixel, x along a row, y up; a pixel position is inside a frame of w by h when 0.5 <= x <= w + 0.5 and 0.5 <= y <= h + 0.5
conventions.projection: the TAN projection and WCS of js/measure/astrometry.js (Prompt 181), a CD matrix in degrees per pixel; no distortion terms; no aberration, no precession, no parallax: a catalogue position is a J2000 (ICRS-aligned) direction moved by proper motion alone
conventions.properMotion: linear in the J2000 unit vector from the catalogue's pmra (which carries cos dec) and pmde, radial velocity and parallax neglected: js/kernels/sky/stars.js starAtEpoch, whose own stated error against ERFA's pmsafe is at most 0.016 arcmin over 1900-2100
conventions.planets: geometric, geocentric, no light-time, J2000 mean equator, from Standish's elements (js/kernels/sky/planets.js geocentricEquatorial), position bound planetProvenance(null, body, jd).boundDeg = 0.2 degree; Mercury to Saturn
conventions.time: a frame's time moved to TT: UTC and UT1 by js/kernels/sky/time.js ttFromUt (UTC taken as UT1, at most 0.9 s apart by the definition of UTC), TAI by +32.184 s, TT as it is, TDB less tdbMinusTt (at most 1.7 ms); TCB and local refuse; the instant is the middle of the exposure when the sidecar says the time is its start or its end and gives the exposure

rules.exposureRule: frames in a count unit (adu, count, electron, photon) must have equal exposures; a rate unit (per second) needs none
rules.resampling: bilinear: an output pixel is NaN when any of its four neighbours in the second frame is outside it or is NaN; the difference is second-frame-resampled minus first-frame, NaN where either is NaN, and is a picture for the eye, never a measurement and never stored

orion.what: The bright-star pack (sky/bright-stars.json, 904 stars, J2000.0 as the pack rounds them) over a 1024 by 1024 frame whose truth WCS is the one of Prompt 181's orion scene, at a time of 2026-01-01T00:00:00 UTC

planets.what: Five planets at five instants given as TT Julian dates

resample.what: A seeded 96 by 72 frame of values uniform in [0, 1000), carried onto a 96 by 72 first-frame grid by a rotation of 2.5 degrees about the frame centre and a shift

centroid.what: A Gaussian star (sigma 2 pixels, amplitude 1000) on a flat sky in a 64 by 64 first frame and, moved by a known rotation and shift, in a second frame; the second carried onto the first

skyMap.what: A first frame and a second frame with their own TAN WCS (a different reference position, rotation and scale); a first-frame pixel carried to the second through the sky

ensemble.what: Random truth per trial, as Prompt 181's ensemble: reference sky position RA uniform 0 to 360 and Dec uniform -60 to 60 degrees, scale log-uniform 0.5 to 60 arcsec per pixel, position angle uniform, parity at random (the affine truth also has an axis ratio within 0.5 percent and a skew within 0.2 degree); 5 to 8 fit stars uniform over [50, 974] squared at least 100 pixels apart, their pixels with Gaussian noise of 0.15 pixel on each axis; the catalogue positions of the five test pixels are exact, and the question is where the fitted WCS puts them

mismatch.what: Matched ensemble trials (affine) whose registration pairs have two pairs swapped, 300 trials, 12 sources over [50, 974] squared, noise 0.05 pixel, a shift of 3.37, -5.81 and a rotation of 0.35 degree

timing.what: The whole pack over a 1024 by 1024 frame; a 1024 by 1024 frame carried by a registration and differenced against another

a1.tangentPoint.what: A catalogue star at the reference position of a WCS lands at CRPIX

a1.roundTrip.what: For a 21 by 21 grid of pixels of the orion truth WCS, a synthetic star pack with a star at each pixel's sky position (no proper motion) comes back from the overlay at that pixel

a2.properMotion.what: A star with pmra 1000 mas/yr (cos dec carried) and pmde 0 at declinations 0, 30, 60 and 80 degrees, ten Julian years after J2000.0: its angular displacement from its catalogue position is 10 arcsec, directed east; and a star with pmra = pmde = 0 does not move

a3.timeScales.what: UTC 2026-01-01T00:00:00 to TT is 69.184 s later (37 leap seconds and 32.184 s) within 1.0 s; TAI to TT is +32.184 s; TT is itself; TDB differs from TT by tdbMinusTt; the ISO, MJD and JD forms of one instant agree; 'start' with a 100 s exposure moves to the middle by +50 s and 'end' by -50 s

a4.frameEdge.what: A star at pixel 0.5001 is listed and one at 0.4999 is not, in x and in y, and the same at the far edge (w + 0.4999 listed, w + 0.5001 not); no listed entry of the orion scene lies outside the frame

a5.cap.what: A synthetic pack of 800 stars all inside the frame, with the limit of 500: exactly the 500 brightest are listed, the count of those left out (300) is reported, and they are in magnitude order

a6.planetOverlay.what: Each planet entry lies at pixelOf(wcs, the kernel's geocentricEquatorial RA and Dec); its bound in degrees is planetProvenance's and its radius in pixels is the bound over the scale

a7.resampleIdentity.what: The identity registration carries a frame onto itself unchanged (a pixel is the same bits wherever all four neighbours exist, which is everywhere), and an integer shift is exact where defined

a8.rotationCentroid.what: The centroid scene: the intensity-weighted centroid of the star in the second frame carried onto the first lies within the bound of the first frame's centroid

a9.difference.what: The difference of identical frames is zero where defined; of a frame and the same plus a constant of 3 it is 3 on every defined pixel; of a frame and the same plus a point source of known amplitude (integer-shifted second frame) its peak is the amplitude

a10.blinkPlan.what: The blink interval is 1000 / rate milliseconds for the rates 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 per second; any other rate is refused; with reduced motion there is no timer and the toggle is manual

b1.oracleStarsJ2000.what: All 904 stars of the pack projected through the orion truth WCS with the epoch at J2000.0 (no proper motion), against astropy.wcs (wcslib) world_to_pixel, pinned: the set of stars inside the frame is the same (stars within 0.001 pixel of the edge excluded and listed) and every pixel position agrees

b1.oracleStarsEpoch.what: The same at 2026-01-01T00:00:00 UTC: astropy SkyCoord.apply_space_motion (rigorous, no parallax, no radial velocity) from J2000.0 to the astropy UTC to TT instant, then wcslib; same set, every pixel position. The bound is 0.18 arcsec at the scene's 90 arcsec a pixel: the proper-motion linearization of 0.1 arcsec stated for the pack's fastest stars and the 1 s of time

b1.oracleTime.what: The kernel's UTC to TT of 2026-01-01T00:00:00 against astropy Time (leap seconds and 32.184 s, no IERS file), pinned, in seconds

b2.oraclePlanets.what: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn at the five instants: the angular separation between the kernel's geocentric position and astropy's get_body with the builtin ephemeris (ERFA plan94) in GCRS, pinned. The bound is the kernel's own stated planet bound, read from planetProvenance, 0.2 degree

b3.oracleResample.what: The seeded 96 by 72 frame carried by the rotation and shift against scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates (order 1, bilinear, 0-based coordinates), pinned: the same defined pixels and values on every pixel whose four neighbours exist

b4.oracleSkyMap.what: A first-frame pixel carried to the second frame through the two WCS (first pixel to sky, sky to second pixel) at 25 grid pixels against astropy.wcs (wcslib) all_pix2world and all_world2pix, pinned, in pixels

b5.oracleAuthentic.what: An authentic frame with catalogue stars: the overlay's pixel for each catalogue star against astropy.wcs given the same solution
b5.oracleAuthentic.status: NOT RUN until Prompt 189 lands an authentic image pack with a catalogue match; nothing was downloaded and nothing fabricated for this leg

c1.coveragePredictionAffine.what: The affine ensemble: z = (fitted pixel of a test star's exact position - its true pixel) / stated sigma of the prediction (the fit's covariance carried to that star's pixel), per axis, at the five test pixels; fraction with |z| < 1 and with |z| < 1.96

c2.coveragePredictionSimilarity.what: The same for a truth that is a similarity and the similarity model

d1.noTimeNoScale.what: A frame with no time: the planets are refused with the code no-time, the stars are listed at the catalogue epoch with the treatment not-moved; a frame whose time scale is TCB or local: the planets are refused with the code time-scale and the stars not moved; a time that does not parse refuses with the code time

d2.noSky.what: A sidecar marked display-only refuses the overlay with the contract's own words and the code display-only; an image with neither a usable header WCS nor a solved calibration refuses with no-wcs; a SIN or SIP header is refused by name by fromHeader, with its code

d3.differenceRefusals.what: Nine constructed pairs, one per code in rules.differenceRefusals, each refused with exactly its code and a reason in words; a quantitative pair of one calibration state, one unit and equal exposures is accepted; a pair in a per-second unit with different exposures is accepted

d4.mismatchedPairs.what: Registration with two pairs swapped: the verdict is inconsistent, and the difference is refused with the code registration, in at least this fraction of the trials

d5.decodedMemory.what: The difference holds four planes (the two frames, the carried frame and the result): 1024 by 1024 is accepted and 2048 by 2048 refused with too-large, by js/dataKinds/limits.js residentFrames; a second frame of another size than the first is refused for the identity tie with the code shape

d6.registrationInherited.what: Fewer than three matched pairs refuse with the kernel's code too-few and no blink alignment is made; pairs whose registration is degenerate refuse with degenerate

e1.authenticFrame.what: An authentic calibrated frame pair with catalogue stars and a moving object, blinked and overlaid under a fixed analysis contract
e1.authenticFrame.status: NOT RUN until Prompt 189; no frame fetched, none simulated

f1.timePack.what: The overlay of the whole pack over the 1024 by 1024 orion frame, in plain Node, milliseconds (a loaded machine runs slow; the bound is generous)

f2.timeResample.what: The 1024 by 1024 second frame carried by the registration and the difference, in plain Node, milliseconds
